name: How close can a home office addition be to a neighbor’s window in dense Los Angeles neighborhoods?

mainEntity.name: What privacy and design problems come up when a new office sits near neighboring homes?
mainEntity.text: What privacy and design problems come up when a new office sits near neighboring homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In dense neighborhoods, privacy and spacing are major design issues. Even when a project technically fits the lot, the placement of windows, doors, and rooflines can create direct views into neighboring homes or reduce natural privacy. That is why the design should consider sight lines, not just property boundaries. Builders often use strategic window placement, frosted glass, landscaping, fencing, or wall orientation to soften the impact. This matters especially for offices intended for video calls or client use, because the space should feel calm and private inside while remaining considerate outside. A good design balances daylight, views, and neighbor privacy instead of maximizing windows everywhere. For properties in tightly built areas, the best office addition is often the one that feels visually quiet from the outside and comfortable from the inside.
acceptedAnswer.description: The design needs to account for setbacks, window placement, privacy, and sight lines so the office does not create an uncomfortable or poorly screened edge condition. In dense neighborhoods, careful layout matters as much as the building itself.
